title: Gated Procedure
description: AIP schema for procedures that run under human approval: a graph of steps where named gates stop the work until an accountable person approves, and the approval is recorded. Covers the procedure's place in a levelled process model, the rules holding across all of its steps, what each step produces, and where it hands off to another skill and returns.

name.description: Identifier for this input or output. A downstream step consumes it by declaring an input of the same name.

type.description: Short type label from the AIP vocabulary: string, integer, float, boolean, object, or list[*]. Not machine-enforced; detailed checks belong in the backing script.

nullable.description: Optional. True when the value may be absent. Defaults to false.

description.description: One-line summary of what this carries, so the graph reads without opening the script.

gate.description: An approval checkpoint. Its presence is what makes a step stop and wait for a person; a step without one is the agent proceeding on its own judgement.

id.description: The gate's name as the method states it, e.g. 'Gate 2 - Business'. The single source for which gate applies when is the change-alignment skill, not this field.

approver_role.description: The role that grants approval. A role, never a person.

presents.description: What the approver is shown, one entry per document or artifact. An approval granted against a summary is an approval of the summary.

recorded_in.description: Where the approval is written down. An approval that isn't recorded didn't happen.

on_changes_requested.description: Which step the procedure returns to when the approver asks for changes.

not_applicable_when.description: The condition under which this gate does not apply. A gate that didn't apply is recorded as N/A with its reason, never deleted.

handoff.description: A switch to another skill that is not an exit: the work continues there and comes back.

skill.description: Name of the skill taking over.

when.description: The verdict or condition that triggers the handoff.

returns.description: What comes back, and which step resumes. Omit only when the handoff genuinely ends this procedure.

name.description: Short kebab-case identifier, unique within this procedure. Other steps reference it via depends_on.

description.description: What the step does. When the step is script-backed, keep this to a one-line summary; the script is the source of truth for the logic.

actor.description: Who performs the step. The method's three roles; the Agent may be an AI or a person.

depends_on.description: Optional. Names of steps that must complete first. Omit for steps that run in list order.

one_of.description: Optional. Mutually exclusive verdicts or alternatives; the agent reaches exactly one and states it. Use where choosing hinges on judging the input, which is what keeps it out of a script.

script.description: Optional. Relative path under scripts/ to the code that executes this step. When present, the script is the source of truth for the logic.

analysis.description: Optional. The judgement the step demands - the criteria applied, not the mechanics. Prose steps only; a script-backed step has none.

uses_template.description: Optional. Relative path under assets/, or the name of the document-template skill that owns the output's shape.

produces.description: Optional. Repository paths this step writes or updates. Makes 'which skill writes this document' answerable without reading the body.

inputs.description: Optional. What this step consumes - outputs of upstream steps, or values supplied from outside.

outputs.description: Optional. What this step produces, consumed downstream by name.

purpose.description: What the procedure encapsulates as a coherent unit of work - the scope it covers and what it adds beyond general agent knowledge. One short paragraph.

trigger_when.description: Conditions under which the agent should consider this skill. Mixed granularity expected - an immediate invocation trigger and a broader applicability context belong in the same list.

do_not_use_when.description: Optional. Conditions under which this skill is the wrong one, sharpening activation against its neighbours.

realizes_process.description: Optional. IDs of the level-2 processes this skill realizes, from the method's process model. A list, because a skill and a process are cut on different axes and bind many-to-many. The full SIPOC lives once, in the process model; this field references it and never restates it. Omit for a skill that realizes no process.

applies_at_depth.description: Optional. Modeling depths at which this procedure applies - 1 Application, 2 Organization, 3 Enterprise. Omit when it applies at all three.

invariants.description: Optional. Rules that hold across every step rather than at one of them. A rule repeated into each step is that rule maintained in several places.

scope_and_approval.description: Optional. Read-only versus write actions, and what the procedure may do without human confirmation. The gates are typed on the steps that carry them; this is the surrounding posture.

steps.description: The steps the agent executes, in list order unless depends_on says otherwise. A step carrying a gate stops until its approver acts.

hands_off_to.description: Optional. Skills this procedure switches to mid-flight and returns from. Handing off is not an exit.

done_when.description: Optional. Checkable conditions that all hold when the procedure is finished.

integrations.description: Optional. How this procedure composes with other skills or workflows, as freeform prose per partner.

partner.description: Name of the partner skill or workflow.

scenarios.description: Optional. Worked examples showing the procedure applied to concrete cases. Documentation, not a runtime decision table.

need.description: The situation the procedure is applied to.

anti_patterns.description: Optional. Concrete corrections to mistakes the agent would otherwise make.
